body.rationale:
Use model 1 of the deposited 2RE9 asymmetric unit, revision 1.4 dated 2024-11-20, determined by X-ray diffraction at 2.10 Å. The coordinate artifact and quality summary identify the same SHA-256, 8c8b9a48cf32d0350327a8c74ecb18bec0ebacb4bdea6f484460fd7b1d5dd89b. I rebuilt the three masks from _atom_site and checked their identities against the inventory. Only coverage and within-chain spatial extent were examined in designing this test. All three pairwise fitting protocols are prospective.

Restrict to label_entity_id 1 and label_asym_id A, B and C. Intersect positive-occupancy atoms across all three chains by (label_seq_id, label_comp_id, label_atom_id) before fitting any pair. With the first chain fixed and the second moving, fit (A,B), (A,C) and (B,C) in deposited Cartesian coordinates. Use equal weight per selected atom, least-squares translation and a proper rotation without scaling, reflection or outlier rejection. Record selected atom and residue counts, the principal angle of the fitted rotation in degrees and the post-fit RMSD over that protocol's own atoms in Å.

The common_backbone reference has 656 N, CA, C and O atoms per chain. The common_ca fit has 164 CA atoms at precisely the same 164 residues. Their contrast isolates the choice of atom representation at fixed residue coverage. For ordered_backbone require all four backbone atoms in all three copies to have occupancy 1 and B_iso_or_equiv ≤40 Å². Its 196 atoms cover 49 residues. Comparing it with common_backbone tests omission of 115 residues at fixed atom types. An RMSD change here can reflect the selected residues' local agreement as well as a change of fitted rotation. The common_ca versus ordered_backbone comparison changes both selections and will also be reported.

Freeze the denominator at the 164 distinct observed residue positions in the union of the three chains. Labels 1–17 of the 181 declared positions lack coordinates throughout, so leave them unfilled and restrict inference to labels 18–181. Require both at least 40 distinct residues and at least 0.25 of the observed union, effectively 41 residues here. This demands several dozen residues for each fit and allows the ordered subset (49/164, 29.88%) to test sensitivity to selective omission. The default 60-residue and 60% gates would exclude it before measurement. The ordered positions span multiple stretches from label 26 to 180 but preferentially sample a compact region. Check that each fit constrains a unique rotation, including at least three noncollinear correspondences. A passing count alone does not establish that.

Freeze comparison bounds of 0.5° in principal rotation angle and 0.15 Å in fitted RMSD. The full Cα sets have radii of gyration near 17.8 Å, where a point at that distance perpendicular to the rotation axis moves about 0.16 Å under a 0.5° rotation. This gives the two screening thresholds comparable physical scales while keeping angle and residual RMSD distinct. Independently rebuild correspondences from the same mmCIF and repeat each rigid fit. Require identical selected keys and agreement within 0.01° and 0.001 Å against the unrounded results for every pair. Those limits allow small numerical differences and are 50 and 150 times tighter than the respective comparison bounds. They measure computational reproducibility.

For each fixed/moving pair tabulate all three protocols' measurements, all three between-protocol absolute differences in each metric, and each metric's range over protocols. Use unrounded values for decisions. These ranges quantify uncertainty due to the specified atom selections. Declare stable when every contrast meets both bounds, or sensitive when any contrast exceeds either bound, conditional on complete coverage-qualified, determined and reproduced fits. If a required fit is missing, underdetermined, below the frozen coverage or fails reproduction, or fewer than two distinct protocols are comparable, return insufficient and retain each observable measurement and individual comparison. Carry the same pairs, mapping, denominator and evaluation into later rounds.

The three chain pairs share coordinates. Treat their differences descriptively. B factors reflect both disorder and refinement, and the truly missing positions have unknown geometry. The outcomes apply to pairwise rotation magnitudes and fitted residuals within this asymmetric unit. A common symmetry axis, solution assembly, binding and activity require independent evidence.

Restrict all fits to model 1, polymer label_entity_id 1 and label_asym_id A, B and C. Match the exact (label_seq_id, label_comp_id, label_atom_id) across all three chains before fitting any pair. The backbone records have a single site per identity. Fit B onto A, C onto A and C onto B by equal-weight least squares with a proper rotation and translation. Use the same correspondence, pair directions, denominator and evaluation in any subsequent round.

Use common_backbone as the reference. It gives 656 positive-occupancy N, CA, C and O sites per chain. The common_ca fit uses 164 positive-occupancy CA sites over the same 164 residues. Comparing these selections measures the effect of including peptide-backbone detail while holding residue coverage fixed. The ordered_backbone fit keeps a residue only if all four backbone sites have occupancy 1 and B_iso_or_equiv ≤40 Å² in every chain. Comparing its 196 sites with common_backbone holds atom types fixed and tests the effect of restricting residue coverage. Its RMSD describes agreement on the retained sites and can change even when the fitted angle changes little.

All three chains have backbone coordinates for label positions 18–181. Positions 1–17 of the 181 declared positions lack coordinates throughout, so their influence cannot be measured. Use the union of 164 observed residues as the denominator and leave missing positions unfilled. The ordered selection omits a further 115 observed residues and retains 49 distributed across several stretches from label position 26 to 180. Freeze a minimum of 49 distinct residues and a minimum fraction of 49/164 (29.878%). These floors retain the entire eligible ordered selection, whereas the default 60 residues and 60% would rule it out before the test. This comparison measures sensitivity to that particular occupancy and B-factor selection. B factors reflect both disorder and refinement, and these residues are a selected subset of the chain.

For each fit report its count, coverage, principal rotation angle in degrees from the proper rotation matrix, and post-fit atom RMSD in Å. For each of the three chain pairs report the absolute angle difference and absolute RMSD difference for all three protocol contrasts, yielding nine comparisons. Also give the range across protocols for each metric and chain pair as a description of selection uncertainty. Freeze the practical comparison bounds at 0.5° and 0.15 Å. For scale, a 0.5° rotation displaces a point 20 Å from the axis by about 0.17 Å. The two cutoffs therefore flag small changes of comparable spatial scale, while testing different features of the fits.

Independently reparse and refit the same atom identities. Check the identity lists, atom counts and residue counts exactly. Require each reproduced angle and RMSD to agree within 0.01° and 0.001 Å, respectively. Identical input coordinates allow tight computational checks, at 1/50 and 1/150 of the respective comparison bounds. Evaluate unrounded differences. Both reproduction and comparison tolerances serve this coordinate screen. Experimental uncertainty in the missing positions is unquantifiable here.

Classify only well-determined, reproduced fits with the frozen coverage. If a requested protocol misses coverage, a fit lacks noncollinear correspondences, reproduction fails, or fewer than two distinct comparable protocols are measured, report insufficient evidence for the overall claim and preserve every observable fit and individual contrast. Otherwise equality at a bound counts as stable for that comparison. All contrasts must pass both bounds for overall stability. One exceedance supports sensitivity. The three pairs share chains and cannot supply independent replicates. The conclusions describe the observed asymmetric-unit coordinates. A common symmetry axis, solution assembly, binding and biological activity would require additional evidence.
